headline: Two Bangladeshis among 12 killed in Riyadh airport attack, 309 injured
summary: Saudi authorities confirmed two Bangladeshi citizens were among the 12 fatalities in Saturday's Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport. The assault also left 309 people injured.
details: Two Bangladeshi citizens were among the 12 people killed in an attack by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi armed group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The attack, which occurred on Saturday, also left 309 people injured.

Houthi senior official Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti claimed responsibility for the attack, stating it was in response to Saudi attacks in Yemen. He alleged that Saudi attacks have also targeted civilian infrastructure.
This marks the third attack on King Khalid International Airport this week, leading to a temporary suspension of airport operations. All flights were diverted to other locations or cancelled.

Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation confirmed the fatalities, which include four Saudis, two Bangladeshis, and one citizen each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.

Eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and injured individuals on the ground inside the airport. Ambulances and helicopters were seen rushing to transport the injured to hospitals, causing significant crowding.

The attack occurred without prior warning, and Saudi Arabia's threat detection and warning systems did not issue any alerts. Earlier this week, two other attacks on the airport had killed four people and severely damaged a Saudi commercial aircraft on the runway.
Medical sources indicated that health officials declared a "serious emergency situation" following the attack, urgently calling in doctors to manage the influx of casualties.

Hours after the Riyadh attack, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led international coalition fighting the Houthis reported a "projectile" strike near King Fahad International Airport in Dammam. Early Sunday, the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile southeast of the capital.

Flight monitoring website Flightradar24 reported that 155 inbound and 161 outbound flights were cancelled, with 222 flights delayed. Several airlines had already suspended or cancelled flights to Riyadh due to previous Houthi attacks this week.

headline_marked: [[Thousands detained]] in Delhi over voter list protests, 4 still held
headline: Thousands detained in Delhi over voter list protests, 4 still held
summary: Indian authorities cracked down on protests against alleged electoral irregularities in Delhi, detaining around 3,000 people. While most have been released, four prominent figures, including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, remain in custo
details: Indian authorities detained approximately 3,000 people in a widespread crackdown on protests in New Delhi. The demonstrations were sparked by alleged electoral irregularities and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. While most detainees have since been released, four individuals remain in custody.

Among those still held are Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, as reported by NDTV. The detentions occurred across the capital on Saturday as police acted to prevent protestors from gathering at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site.

Several high-profile political figures were initially detained, including four former chief ministers: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar. The Indian broadcaster stated that most of these leaders were released by Saturday night.

CJP founder Dipke, along with leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were reportedly detained directly from their plane upon landing in Delhi. A personal tragedy unfolded for Dipke while in custody, as his paternal grandmother passed away in Maharashtra.

Police indicated that Dipke was informed he could leave to attend his grandmother's funeral, but his release status remained unclear by Saturday evening. Despite the crackdown, the CJP has pledged to continue daily marches to Jantar Mantar, while police maintain that heavy security measures will persist. The Congress-led INDIA bloc has also announced a protest for Monday.
